comparisons.peer_topic: Variable Rate Demand Obligations Antitrust Litigation Status
comparisons.peer_summary: GS&Co. is a defendant in a consolidated putative class action alleging a conspiracy to manipulate the market for variable rate demand obligations (VRDOs) through federal antitrust and state law claims. While Group Inc. was dismissed in 2019 and various state law and fiduciary duty claims against GS&Co. were dismissed by the district court in 2020 and 2022, the federal antitrust claims remain active as the proceedings are stayed pending an interlocutory appeal of the 2023 class certification grant by the Second Circuit.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and GS disclose status updates on consolidated antitrust class actions where federal claims survived motions to dismiss while other claims were removed, with proceedings impacted by appellate activity. C reports that a third amended complaint in the Mexican Government Bonds litigation had motions to dismiss filed by defendants (Banamex) in July 2024, following prior dismissals of claims against C affiliates. GS reports that in the VRDO litigation, federal antitrust claims against GS&Co. survived multiple motions to dismiss in 2020 and 2022, and the case is stayed pending an interlocutory appeal of the class certification grant to the Second Circuit. Both disclosures highlight the persistence of antitrust claims despite partial dismissals and active appellate or pretrial litigation phases.

sentences.text: On July 29, 2024, certain defendants, including Banamex, filed a motion to dismiss the third amended complaint.

On November 2, 2020, the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss, dismissing the state common law claims against GS&Co., but denying dismissal of the federal antitrust law claims.

On June 28, 2022, the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss, dismissing the state breach of fiduciary duty claim against GS&Co., but declining to dismiss any portion of the federal antitrust law claims.

sentences.text: In December 2019, plaintiffs filed an amended complaint against Banamex and other market makers in the Mexican sovereign bond market.

The amended complaint alleges a conspiracy to fix prices in the Mexican sovereign bond market, asserts antitrust and unjust enrichment claims, and seeks treble damages, restitution, and injunctive relief.

On November 2, 2020, the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss the consolidated complaint, dismissing state law claims, but denying dismissal of the U.S. antitrust claims.
On September 21, 2023, the court granted plaintiffs' motion for class certification.
On February 5, 2024, the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit granted leave to appeal that decision.
